problem: Compute-in-memory accelerators degrade neural network accuracy due to hardware-induced weight perturbations from noise and device drift during edge inference.
approach: Diversity-aware Weight Perturbation (DWP) uses an immune-system-inspired method that emulates selection by exploiting prediction disagreement under diverse noise to adaptively weight samples and build robustness.
contribution: DWP-trained models achieve over 15% accuracy improvements under severe weight perturbations and maintain 90% inference accuracy over simulated one-year CIM operation.

problem: Autonomous agents with fixed action spaces cannot generalize across diverse tasks and suffer from compounding errors in decoupled policy execution.
approach: DeepHA unifies heterogeneous action spaces via a hierarchical architecture, uses Chain-of-Action reasoning to structure high-level actions as guidance for low-level controls, and compresses context via KV caching for efficiency.
contribution: DeepHA establishes state-of-the-art on 800+ Minecraft tasks, demonstrating superior generalization in complex multi-step planning with 75% context length reduction.

problem: It is unclear when ordinal preference-based solution concepts in games can predict the long-run behavior of payoff-driven no-regret learning dynamics.
approach: The paper characterizes the relationship between preference graphs and dynamically stable sets, showing that preference stability is necessary but not sufficient, and introducing leaklessness to capture additional payoff-drift conditions.
contribution: The work proves dynamic stability equivalence for subgames and identifies conditions under which payoff-based leaklessness guarantees stability.

problem: Existing Nash regret bounds for linear bandits are suboptimal in ambient dimension, limiting fair multi-armed bandit algorithms.
approach: New analytical tools yield order-optimal Nash regret bounds; p-means regret framework unifies fairness and utility objectives as a meta-algorithm over existing bandit strategies.
contribution: Order-optimal Nash regret bound in linear bandits; framework instantiated with Phased Elimination and UCB showing sublinear p-means regret across all p values.

problem: Full-library surrogate inference is a computational bottleneck when screening candidates from billion-scale discrete molecular spaces under expensive evaluations.
approach: BOBA treats library partitions as arms in a multi-armed bandit, adaptively allocating inference and evaluations across partitions based on empirical promise while maintaining exploration.
contribution: Establishes tunable tradeoff between screening performance and inference cost, enabling practical optimization over current billion-scale molecular libraries.

problem: Negative-label-guided OOD detection in vision-language models lacks understanding of effectiveness in open-world scenarios where negative labels diverge from real OOD data.
approach: Energy-based framework quantifies label margins as energy functions; Rényi divergence refines potential distributions to avoid over-pessimism and reduce outlier sensitivity.
contribution: Establishes state-of-the-art OOD detection with theoretical analysis showing existing methods suffer from over-pessimism and proving Rényi divergence alleviates the problem.

problem: Physics-informed diffusion models enforcing PDE constraints only on outputs leave intermediate representations unconstrained, causing shortcut learning under shifted boundary conditions.
approach: REPA-P aligns intermediate features with physical states via first-principles residuals using lightweight projection heads decoded into physical quantities with PDE residual losses.
contribution: Reduces physics residuals by up to 66.4%, improves out-of-distribution robustness by up to 49.3%, and accelerates convergence by up to 2× with zero inference overhead.

problem: Diffusion-based dataset distillation lacks direct prototype matching due to indirect denoising objectives and generates target-agnostic samples that drift from task distributions.
approach: ProtoVAR uses coarse-to-fine Visual AutoRegressive modeling with injected multi-scale class prototypes to enforce representativeness while preserving diversity.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art distillation performance with comparable or lower computational cost than diffusion-based approaches.

problem: Existing structure prediction models fail to capture functionally relevant protein dynamics across conformational states in biological contexts.
approach: ProMiSE benchmark integrates multiple conformational change mechanisms (intrinsic, ligand-induced, protein-induced) and evaluates state-of-the-art models including AlphaFold3.
contribution: Reveals that current models exhibit limited multi-state sampling and insensitivity to biological context, with training-data exposure shifting predictions toward dominant states.

problem: Federated learning with noisy labels is exacerbated by heterogeneous label-noise types and ratios across clients, degrading model robustness.
approach: FedGR exploits the global model's slow memorization of noisy labels via three collaborative modules that rectify noisy labels and regularize local training in a self-contained manner.
contribution: Consistently outperforms eight baselines across three federated label-noise benchmarks, even under severe noise and data heterogeneity.

problem: Obtaining generalization guarantees for reinforcement learning is challenging due to Markov dependencies in sequential data violating independence assumptions.
approach: Novel PAC-Bayesian bound explicitly accounts for Markov mixing time; PB-SAC algorithm optimizes the bound during training to guide exploration.
contribution: Provides non-vacuous generalization certificates for off-policy algorithms like Soft Actor-Critic while maintaining competitive performance.

problem: Retrieval-augmented generation suffers from substantial latency due to synchronous retrieval and existing asynchronous approaches rely on heuristic coordination.
approach: Predictive prefetching framework predicts when to trigger retrieval and what to retrieve using three components that exploit semantic precursors in generation dynamics.
contribution: Achieves up to 43.5% end-to-end latency reduction and 62.4% improvement in time-to-first-token while maintaining answer quality.

problem: 3D molecular diffusion generates inconsistently across sizes because larger molecules form coarse structures earlier due to larger spatial scales.
approach: Scaling the Prior (StP) rescales the prior distribution by molecular size to normalize learning across sizes and harmonize denoising trajectories.
contribution: Generates high-quality molecules with size-consistent generative patterns across diverse molecular sizes.

problem: Noise schedules for pixel diffusion are typically handcrafted and require manual tuning across different image resolutions.
approach: Principled per-image noise schedule design based on spectral properties derives theoretical bounds on efficacy of minimum and maximum noise levels.
contribution: Eliminates redundant diffusion steps and improves generative quality particularly in the low-step inference regime.

problem: Single-cell perturbation modeling is hindered because gene expression is dominated by perturbation-invariant information while perturbation-specific signals are sparse.
approach: PerturbedVAE explicitly separates perturbation-specific information from dominant invariant structure using a framework with identifiability analysis.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance with significant gains in out-of-distribution combinatorial predictions and interpretable perturbation-response programs.

problem: Integrating GNNs and LLMs on text-attributed graphs requires achieving well-aligned representations without sufficient distributional constraints.
approach: ERAlign uses energy-based models to project GNN and LLM embeddings in shared latent space with layer-wise alignment quantified via distance metrics and optimized via EBM objectives.
contribution: Obtains state-of-the-art performance on TAG datasets with energy-discrepancy training enabling higher efficiency and reduced landscape distortion.

problem: Existing adaptation methods for diffusion models incur high computational overhead from training and rely on restrictive assumptions about reward differentiability.
approach: DOIT leverages Doob's h-transform to realize measure transport from pre-trained distribution to high-reward target via dynamic correction to sampling without modifying the model.
contribution: Provides convergence guarantees to target high-reward distribution and outperforms state-of-the-art on conditional synthesis and trajectory sampling.

problem: Native 4K video generation faces quadratic computational explosion from full-attention as spatiotemporal resolution increases.
approach: T3 retrofits pretrained full-attention models via multi-scale weight-sharing window attention and hierarchical blocking without altering core architecture.
contribution: Accelerates native 4K video generation by more than 10× with +4.29 VQA and +0.08 VTC performance improvements.

problem: LLM serving frameworks produce different outputs for identical inputs across different tensor parallel sizes due to floating-point non-associativity.
approach: Tree-Based Invariant Kernels (TBIK) enforce consistent reduction order across and within GPUs via custom matrix multiplication and reduction kernels.
contribution: Achieves bit-wise deterministic inference across different tensor parallel sizes and zero probability divergence between rollout and training in RL.

problem: Training-data attribution for vision generative models typically scores individual examples but practitioners need group-level answers.
approach: GUDA approximates Leave-One-Group-Out counterfactuals via machine unlearning applied to a full-data model, quantifying influence using likelihood-based scoring.
contribution: Identifies primary contributing groups more reliably than semantic similarity and gradient approaches with ~100× speedup over LOGO retraining.

problem: Image-to-video diffusion models frequently produce motion violating physical laws despite using many denoising steps.
approach: PhaseLock extracts motion priors from 2-step inference and enforces them via Latent Delta Guidance throughout denoising to prevent phase degradation.
contribution: Improves physical consistency by average 6.2 points with negligible overhead (1.06× time, 1.02× memory) while maintaining visual fidelity.

problem: Existing synthesis pipelines for reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards are bottlenecked by expert-written code and fixed templates.
approach: SSLogic uses an agentic meta-synthesis framework where LLM agents iteratively author and refine Generator-Validator pairs via Generate-Validate-Refine loops.
contribution: Starting from 400 seed families, two evolution rounds yield 953 families and 21,389 instances with gains of SynLogic +5.2, AIME25 +3.0, BBH +5.5.

problem: Policy optimization in contextual MDPs under general offline function approximation lacks regret bounds with optimal dependence on state and action spaces.
approach: OPO-CMDP introduces a policy optimization algorithm achieving near-optimal regret through careful interaction between offline function approximation and policy learning.
contribution: Achieves regret bound with optimal dependence on state and action spaces, improving over prior state-of-the-art.

problem: Watermarks embedded for AI-generated text detection trivially fail when users access multiple models through simple ensemble averaging.
approach: WASH solves practical ensemble challenges via vocabulary alignment and tokenization harmonization across heterogeneous models.
contribution: Averaging 3-5 models suppresses detection z-scores below 2 and reduces TPR@5%FPR below 50% while improving quality by 27.5%.

problem: Multimodal large language models cannot directly process structured non-visual data like human skeletons.
approach: SkeletonLLM translates skeleton sequences into MLLMs' native visual modality via differentiable renderer DrAction, with cooperative training combining causal reasoning distillation and discriminative finetuning.
contribution: Demonstrates universal skeleton understanding with strong generalization across recognition, captioning, reasoning, and cross-format transfer tasks.

problem: Clustered multitask learning with heterogeneous nuisance components violates aligned feature spaces and homogeneous task structure assumptions.
approach: Adaptive fused orthogonal estimator integrates Neyman-orthogonal losses with data-driven pairwise fusion penalties and adaptive aggregation.
contribution: Achieves exact recovery of latent clustering and pooled parametric convergence rates proportional to cluster size with asymptotic oracle equivalence.

problem: Watermarking schemes for language model attribution lack formal abstraction for reasoning about attribution decisions.
approach: Ideal attribution mechanisms formalize attribution via ledgers (append-only logs of interactions) with deterministic decisions based on explicit selection criteria.
contribution: Provides unified language for reasoning about watermarking guarantees and clarifies which properties are attainable for practical schemes.

problem: Deep neural network time-series forecasting models deployed as black-box APIs are vulnerable to adversarial attacks that remain largely underexplored.
approach: TSFAdv embeds frequency-domain priors into Natural Evolution Strategies for sensitivity-guided gradient estimation under query constraints.
contribution: Achieves 38.78% median DTW improvement and 26.47% median SME improvement under 200-query budget across seven state-of-the-art architectures.

problem: Vision-language-action models assume task-relevant objects are always visible, leading to brittle reactive behaviors when targets fall outside the camera field of view.
approach: SOMA equips VLAs with persistent spatial memory constructed from multi-view observations, with components for memory construction, refinement, and retrieval.
contribution: Improves task success on out-of-vision manipulation tasks with faster target localization and near one-shot grasping under partial observability.

problem: Test-time guidance for generative models faces limitations with non-differentiable rewards, complex landscapes, and lacks theoretical guarantees.
approach: Source Parallel Tempering (SPT) operates in source space leveraging its simpler geometry via local exploration kernel and parallel tempering for barrier crossing.
contribution: Provides error bound linking training approximation to test-time performance and significantly improves over state-of-the-art on conditional synthesis.

problem: Existing optimizers like Muon are only half-aligned with maximal update parametrization, controlling updates but allowing weights to drift.
approach: Spectral Sphere Optimizer (SSO) enforces strict module-wise spectral constraints on both weights and updates via steepest descent on the spectral sphere.
contribution: Outperforms AdamW and Muon across diverse architectures with improved MoE router load balancing, suppressed outliers, and strictly bounded activations.

problem: Multi-agent offline learning struggles with catastrophic forgetting and plasticity loss when facing sequential tasks with exponential skill space.
approach: COMAD discovers skills via auto-encoder transformation of mixed behavior data and constructs skill-augmented policy learning with reusability estimation.
contribution: Continually expands skill library to mitigate interference, achieving superior forward and backward transfer across MARL benchmarks.

problem: Evaluating LLM conversational quality at human scale relies on synthetic metrics rather than human sources, falling short for multi-turn dialogue.
approach: UPHELD provides reference-full benchmark with hundreds of professionally-authored human dialogues and 36,000+ per-turn human annotations across 30,000+ turns.
contribution: Develops Mixture-of-Judges framework improving correlation with human judgment by ~30% over existing automatic metrics and LLM-as-a-judge approaches.

problem: Virtual screening on ultra-large combinatorial synthesis libraries routinely scores fewer than 0.1% of compounds, missing many high-scoring molecules.
approach: APEX uses neural surrogate exploiting CSL structure to enable full enumeration of approximate top-k sets on consumer GPU within a minute.
contribution: Enables exact retrieval of approximate top-k compounds and allows amortization across changing constraints and objectives.

problem: Domain adaptation under label shift challenges existing methods that rely on aligned feature spaces or homogeneous task structures.
approach: RDALS adapts via moment-matching linear system using LDA in deep latent space, providing rigorous finite-sample and generalization error bounds.
contribution: Significantly outperforms baselines in both data-scarce and extreme-shift regimes with superior robustness and accuracy.

problem: Classification error scales as a power law in number of classes, but the structure of optimal decomposition for chain-of-thought remains unclear.
approach: Theory shows classification error reduces via tree-structured decomposition of overall task into smaller classification problems, identifying critical degree threshold and optimal depth.
contribution: Identifies threshold below which thinking is detrimental and optimal depth minimizing error, proving error cannot be surpassed by increasing depth.

problem: Grokking (onset of generalization long after overfitting) lacks rigorous quantitative bounds relating generalization delay to training hyperparameters.
approach: End-to-end grokking results for over-parameterized ridge regression with gradient descent showing stages of overfitting, poor generalization, and recovery.
contribution: Provides first rigorous quantitative bounds on grokking time in terms of hyperparameters, proving grokking is consequence of specific conditions, not inherent failure mode.

problem: Iterated empirical risk minimization with prediction-dependent losses introduces intricate statistical dependencies across samples distinguishing from classical ERM.
approach: Sharp asymptotic characterization of test error for linear models trained with convex losses on Gaussian mixture data despite data reuse.
contribution: Removes oracle and sample-splitting assumptions in active learning, uncovering fundamental budget allocation tradeoff and double-descent driven purely by data selection.

problem: Causes of representational similarity across machine learning models remain underexplored despite numerous works documenting the similarity.
approach: Evaluates effects of dataset overlap and task overlap on model similarity through experiments across model sizes and modalities.
contribution: Finds dataset and task overlap positively associated with higher representational similarity, with greater similarity linked to increased adversarial transferability.

problem: Self-supervised learning for time-series has high computational costs and relies on assumptions that do not hold across diverse temporal dynamics.
approach: Di-COT avoids augmentation by contrasting informative substructures via stochastic partition of windows into overlapping sub-blocks with length-independent loss computation.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on six large-scale datasets with substantially reduced training time and no reliance on augmentation.
